newsitem.title: USA: Jenny Craig must warn weight loss is only temporary.
newsitem.headline: Jenny Craig must warn weight loss is only temporary.

text.p: From now on, Jenny Craig Inc. must warn consumers its weight loss methods are usually only temporary, the federal government said Thursday.
The provision is one of several announced by the Federal Trade Commission settling deceptive advertising charges brought against the weight loss company in 1993.

Claims in most ads will have to include the statement: "For many dieters, weight loss is temporary." Jenny Craig will also have to disclose the average weight loss maintenance for consumers, the commission said.

The government agency also focused on testimonials based on experiences atypical of most Jenny Craig clients. Testimonials about highly successful maintenance of weight loss must now be accompanied by the phrase: "This result is not typical. You may be less successful."

In the past, some ads suggested dieters could lose all the weight they wanted for $49, although the actual costs could run into hundreds of dollars. Jenny Craig must end that practice, the commission said.
In a statement, Jenny Craig said, "The consent agreement does not suggest the company violated any law or regulation and it does not involve payment by the company of any financial damages."
But Jenny Craig faces civil penalties of up to $11,000 per day if it fails to live up to its promises, FTC spokeswoman Bonnie Jansen said.
Jenny Craig President C. Joseph LaBonte said: "After nearly six years of discussions, we're pleased to put this matter behind us."

But apparently the settlement could have been reached years ago. FTC spokeswoman Jansen noted that similar settlements were reached in 1993 with three other weight loss companies. Jenny Craig did not settle, and charges were filed.
While the consent agreement itself makes no comment about the company's past practices, Jansen noted that it settles charges of deceptive advertising.
"Jenny Craig has agreed not to misrepresent the performance, safety or customer endorsement of any weight loss programme and to have scientific data to back up future claims," the FTC said.

The FTC vote was 4-0. The public will have 60 days to comment to the FTC, Office of the Secretary, 6th and Pennsylvania Ave. NW, Washington DC 20580. The public can also reach the FTC through the World Wide Web, at http://www.ftc.gov.
Similar charges against Weight Watchers were pulled from litigation a week ago pending the possibility of a settlement with the FTC.
